items.s: The Highgate "Open." Report and result of the Highgate open walk, where Belgrave won the scratch team with 18 pts. and Harry Churcher beat Vic Stone (Poly.) by fifteen seconds; a few printed handicap times (H. G. Clayton, P. G. Wright, F. H. Elson, W. G. True) do not agree with actual time less allowance, and Clayton's team column is printed "1" where others have I, A or B. With our four scoring men in the first seven positions, we registered a win in the first "open" in no uncertain manner. Harry Churcher continued his unbeaten record of last season, to win by fifteen seconds from Vic Stone (Poly.). Both these men strayed off the course at three miles; as our man was leading he went further off than his rival. On regaining the course, Harry was a few yards to the bad; these he made up and won as stated. One interesting feature of the race was the performance of the R.A.F. (Halton) team. Making their début in "opens," they provided the winner of the individual handicap (who finished 8th) and took second place in the team handicap. Perhaps their success will prompt other sections of the forces to encourage road-walking. Their progress will be watched with interest by all. We were pleased to see our old friend Bert Field competing. He had come down from Birmingham with the Dunlop W.C. Our teams were unsuccessful in the handicap, perhaps that's just as well, for if we monopolise the handicaps, we shall soon all be on scratch! RESULTS. Winner of Handicap: W. A. items.s: The Enfield "Open"—12th November. Report and results of the Enfield open walk on 12th November, won by Harry Churcher, with Belgrave winning the scratch team race (the handicap team table prints third place twice). Our run of success in "opens" was continued in the Enfield "Open" race. Harry Churcher led the field home to win comfortably from Joe Coleman. Colin Sutton and Percy Wright completed our team in fifth and sixth positions. Charlie Churcher was hot on Percy's heels in seventh position—it seems that to be in one of our winning teams in an "open," you must make sure of your place by getting in the first four. Hard luck, Charlie! Leicester W.C. deservedly gained second place. The third place went to our "B" team, which, as far as the scoring went, consisted of "Juniors" Eddie Heather, Syd Roberts, Charlie Speechley and Harry Thaxter. This certainly augurs well for the "Junior" next March. Frank Elson deserves our congratulations on the way he is fighting to attain the speed which he had a few years back. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: Walking notes on the good start to the road season, Harry Churcher's form, the coming R.W.A. Junior Championship and forthcoming walking fixtures.
e: London Tram and Trolley Bus S.A. Open
items.s: With The Walkers. Walking notes on the good start to the road season, Harry Churcher's form, the coming R.W.A. Junior Championship and forthcoming walking fixtures. The Road season has started well for us and gives us hopes that we shall again win all the Open 7 and 10 miles scratch team races. Numbers, too, are good, and it is gratifying to see that even if our first four men home were eliminated, we should still have men prominent enough to challenge, and even win, team honours. * * * * * Harry Churcher has found his form, and may well repeat last year's record when he won every "7" and "10" in the London area. We hope he will crown his athletic career by winning the A.A.A. 7 miles title next April, and so become the first Belgrave man to win an A.A.A. Championship. * * * * * Our strength at the moment is shown in the Enfield A.C. Open race result, where it will be seen that our Captain, Charlie Churcher, finished seventh and yet did not score in the winning team. We finished nine walkers in the first eighteen places, and our "B" team was placed third in the scratch team race. * * * * * To be strong and successful now is very pleasing, but how shall we be placed in a few years' time? All the indications are that we have among our young walkers many who will do extremely well in a few years' time, but we would again emphasize the necessity of introducing and training new walkers. * * * * * At this early date it is impossible to form any accurate opinion of our chances in the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship, to be held next March in the Manchester area. It is certain, however, that we shall have a worthy team, and one which may well gain our second successive win. Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit. * * * * * Walkers are reminded of the Club Junior Championship at 7 miles for the "Horwood" Cup, open to all Club members possessing the R.W.A. "Junior" qualifications. This will take place on December 17th, and a sealed handicap will be held in conjunction. This event has been postponed a week from the date originally planned, December 10th. * * * * * A three miles Walk handicap will be included in the Boxing Day meeting to be held at Battersea Park. Entries have been poor in recent years, and unless numbers improve, this race may disappear from our programme. Those with a "distance" interest will be competing in the Godstone and back race (18¾ miles) on Boxing Day. Full particulars may be had from the Walk Hon. Secretary. In the New Year we have the Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. Open 7 miles race on January 21st. The "Berman" Cup, which we hold, will be awarded to the winning scratch team. The following Saturday we hold the Club 10 miles Championship, and in conjunction with this event will be a sealed handicap and match versus Metropolitan Police W.C. and Surrey A.C. The third successive Saturday's racing will find us at Bellingham, participating in the Open race promoted by the London Tram and Trolley Bus S.A. On February 18th we shall compete in the Valentine's S.C. Open 10 miles race from their quarters at Chadwell Heath. A fortnight later follows the Junior Championship at 10 miles at Manchester. All entries and requests for information should be addressed to— A. A. HARLEY, 39, Roxborough Avenue, Isleworth, Mx. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: L. G. Bennett reviews the sprinters' 1938 season (Inter-Club relays, Southern Counties sprint relay, Middlesex standards) and invites sprinters to winter training with coach F. Stampfl.
items.s: The Sprinters And The Future. L. G. Bennett reviews the sprinters' 1938 season (Inter-Club relays, Southern Counties sprint relay, Middlesex standards) and invites sprinters to winter training with coach F. Stampfl. It is with great pleasure that, on entering into my twelfth season with the Club, I can look forward with so much confidence and optimism, so far as the Sprinters are concerned. The confidence in this section, which I expressed in a 1937 Magazine was not, in view of last year's results, in any way over-optimistic. I really must congratulate every man who represented the Club in 1938, also those who entered the handicaps and put up such good and enthusiastic showings. The spirit existing in the Sprinting Section is enthusiastic to a degree, and this has been shown by the keen competition to gain places in the teams. Now a word or two regarding last season's results. First of all the Sprinters gained maximum points in the Inter-Club Relay matches. This is, I think, the first time this has been accomplished by Belgrave. The times were remarkably good and justified the large margins by which the Club won each race. Next, a weakened team entered the Southern Counties Sprint Championships. True, the Club were lucky to reach the final, but here we finished fourth, with inches separating us from second and third positions, after having drawn lane, one which was waterlogged after heavy rain. As our first attempt this was a fine effort. Congratulations to Messrs. Skelley, Mewes, Pritchard and Blunden, who formed the team. (Congratulations also to Skelley on having his shorts passed by a Southern A.A.A. representative!). Remarkable results were obtained in open relay races. The sprinters all did their part, showing what fine Club-men they are. I must have a croak about Cadogan A.C. In the Middlesex County Championships four sprinters—Botwright, Wiley, Pritchard and yours truly, Bennett—entered and all gained County Standards. Botwright and Wiley also gained Southern Standards. These two, not forgetting Pack, were chosen to represent Middlesex County. The junior sprinters have shown a great improvement in ability and enthusiasm, and I do welcome most warmly those who have now reached the senior stage. You are the members who, by your example, strict training, and keenness will help to keep the Club at the top of the tree in athletics for many years to come. Your responsibilities are heavy. Well, let us look at the lessons we have learned during the past season. First of all, we must train strictly, regularly and with enthusiasm if we want to gain places in the Club teams. Secondly, we must all indulge in baton-changing practice. At the end of the year the teams had improved a great deal, but not enough. Now, I must pass on to Winter training. Here I recommend you to come over to Belgrave Hall every Saturday between 2-45 and 3 p.m. The sprinters have a special pack and a short cross-country run is enjoyed by all. This is one of the finest ways in which a sprinter can keep fit during the Winter. I have encouraged cross-country running for sprinters for several seasons past, and now the famous coach to the Club, Herr. F. Stampfl, has given his endorsement to this. Sprinters may also make use of Herr Stampfl's services if they go to Belgrave Hall on Wednesdays at 7-15 p.m. Ordinary road training facilities are also available on Tuesdays and Thursdays at the "Rising Sun" at 7-15 p.m. This Winter training has proved very useful to the following members, who ran so well last season: S. Botwright, S. Blunden, T. Wiley, A. Mewes, W. Timberlake, F. Simmonds, "Tubby" Smith, Laing, Reynolds and many others. Come over next Saturday and enjoy the good-fellowship which is fostered so much on these runs. To new members, I say that if I can be of any assistance to you, please write and let me know. Here's wishing you the best of luck, and I hope that you will all attend our Socials and Dances, which are announced elsewhere. L. G. BENNETT, 30, Applegarth Road, W.14. L. G. Bennett L. G. items.sum: Notice of Herr Stampfl's Wednesday exercise classes at Belgrave Hall for track and field men.
items.s: Winter Training. Notice of Herr Stampfl's Wednesday exercise classes at Belgrave Hall for track and field men. This is essentially for, but not confined to, track and field events men, whose Winter training is usually restricted. The Club has engaged Herr Stampfl to conduct an exercise class at Belgrave Hall on Wednesdays at 7-30 p.m. The exercises are designed not only for keeping fit, but to educate oneself to achieve greater athletic efficiency. Herr Stampfl, although he has been in this country only a short while, has established himself as a coach of the first rank. Having been a champion in recent years, he is well acquainted with the modern ideas for training. He is himself popular with those with whom he has been in contact, and those who have attended his classes were soon affected with his enthusiasm, and attend regularly. He will be unable to attend after January, but the Hall will be open on Wednesdays for the exercises to be continued until the evenings permit the normal outdoor summer training. F. Stampfl Herr Stampfl coach engaged by the Club Herr Stampfl Belgrave Hall

items.label: March 1939
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the English Cross-country and R.W.A. Junior wins, the Southern, international selections, new members, new field and track captains and F. G. Thomson's A.A.A. election.
items.s: The Hon. Secretary's Commentary. The Hon. Secretary's notes on the English Cross-country and R.W.A. Junior wins, the Southern, international selections, new members, new field and track captains and F. G. Thomson's A.A.A. election. The Hon. Secretary's Commentary. As we go to press comes wonderful news of the winning of the English Cross-country Championship at Manchester. A week earlier our walkers had won the R.W.A. Junior Championship, also at Manchester; and we congratulate both our runners and walkers upon their Championship successes in the North. Justice will be done to these races in our next issue. Meanwhile, well done! * * * * * Heartiest congratulations to Ted Stimpson and Arthur Penny upon being selected for the English Cross-country team to participate in the International event at Cardiff. Our best wishes go with them * * * * * Since our Annual General Meeting we have elected many new members. To R. G. Griffin, R. E. Jeal, H. N. Little, K. J. Winton, H. J. Dickinson, C. H. Dennis, W. M. Butt, J. F. Appleby, B. C. Leeden, J. F. Harding, C. H. Lloyd, A. H. Lomas, J. R. Gibb, J. McDonald, W. D. Buckley, W. E. Budden, P. W. Edwards, A. W. Edwards, L. D. Harris, C. G. Herridge, S. D. Richards, R. E. Duffett, H. B. Halls, K. Moe, J. S. Rowell and A. P. Stevenson we extend a very cordial welcome, and trust they will be with us for years to come. Some of the foregoing have already shown they have ability, and good fellowship, and by now are well established Belgrave Harriers. We would single out for a special welcome, Knut Moe, a Norwegian visitor, who will be with us only for a few months. * * * * * Congratulations to Harry Churcher upon continuing his amazing sequence of successes in Open Walks. Influenza prevented him from competing in the Valentine's Open Walk, or undoubtedly Harry would have scored another win and completed two full seasons without defeat in Open road walks. * * * * * Our spirited attempt to regain the "Southern" Cross-country title did not succeed but we had the satisfaction of taking third place and finishing within nine points of the winners, despite the fact that we were not at full strength. Tom Carter and Ted Stimpson gave a splendid display of running and should appear in England's team later in the year. A word of praise also to our Captain, Bert Footer, who travelled to the race as a reserve, but when circumstances forced him to turn out, called upon his store of experience and determination with such good effect that he was our fourth man to score, in 25th position * * * * * Our walking teams have managed to win scratch team race after race, and we hope to have similar success in the Championship events. Our all-round strength during the last two seasons must be without parallel, and if present enthusiasm and ability continue, we should have many further years of success in store. * * * * * We have a new Field Events Captain in Charlie Jones, who will receive capable assistance from L. Jackson, W. Sutton, H. M. Quackenbos, R. E. Jeal, S. Jones and others. With a new season about to begin, it is hoped that all members will co-operate with T. C. Jones and help him to build up a section from which champions and A.A.A. standard men will flow, and that they will continue to represent the Club with distinction and in keeping with the reputation the Club has earned in other branches of our sport. * * * * * A new Track Captain in Frank Webb will also require the help and consideration of all members. At the present moment our Summer programme is being planned, and it is likely to be a very heavy one. All track men are asked to support the Club handicaps. New members are invited, and requested to make themselves known to the Club officials and their fellow-members. Any member invited to represent the Club and unable to do so MUST notify the Captain in good time. It is a duty he owes himself as well as the Club. These points should be borne in mind by every Club-member. If every member resolves that he will not fail in these respects, we may expect the progress that the efforts of the Committee and the Club's hard workers deserve. * * * * * We were pleased that the Club's nomination to the Southern Committee of the A.A.A.—Mr. F. G. Thomson—was again duly elected, finishing seventh in the list of twenty successful candidates on this occasion. We are sure Mr. Thomson's efforts are appreciated at Crown Court Chambers, as is his work on behalf of the Club. * * * * * The Club is represented on other governing Athletic bodies as follows :— Road Walking Assn.—F. G. Thomson (Past President), A. A. Harley (Committee). Southern Counties C.C. Assn.—H. Parker (Committee). South of the Thames C.C. Assn.—W. H. Hare (Past President), H. Parker (Past President), E. A. Duffett (Committee). Surrey County A.A.A.—F. G. Thomson (Vice-President), H. Parker (Committee), J. G. Coleman (Committee). Middlesex County A.A.A. (as members of Cadogan A.C.)—A. A. Harley (Vice-President and Vice-Chairman), F. R. Webb (Committee). * * * * * The Club Track programme is rapidly taking shape. The dates allocated to us by the L.C.C. appear elsewhere. The Inter-Club relays v. Epsom H., Mitcham A.C. and Croydon H. will take place on May 10th, and the "Doris Shield" Competition v. Ashcombe St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley H. on June 7th. The Club 3 miles Track championship will probably take place on July 31st. We have a very full programme of inter-club fixtures to fulfil on other grounds, and a series of Division II Southern Amateur Athletic League track races and Division I Field Events in which to participate. Additionally, we shall be represented in all the principal track competitions, such as the "Reading Gazette Trophy" competition, the "Waddilove Bowl" Competition at Birmingham, the "Kinnaird Trophy" Competition, and many other events of importance. It is hoped to issue the Club Summer fixture list towards the end of April. Members are particularly requested to note the date of the Ponders End Fête and Gala—July 15th—as at this meeting last year we won two trophies—for the Mile Relay and Three Miles Team Race—and we shall try and defend these with our strongest teams against all comers. * * * * * A suggestion has been made by Surrey Walking Club that we should meet them at cricket on one evening during the Summer. The Hon. Secretary would be glad to hear from any members who are interested. * * * * * The National Fitness Organiser of the Amateur Athletic Association, Mr. C. F. R. Hilton, has arranged for an athletic camping site to be open in Devon from July 3rd until the end of August. The site is situated 8 miles from Exeter and 5 miles from Dawlish and transport will be provided free from these towns to the Camp. The charge, including board and accommodation, will not exceed £1 per head per week. There will be a staff in attendance to do all cooking, etc., but those attending will be expected to perform some duties in connection with the maintenance of the Camp. A qualified coaching staff will be in attendance. Members interested should get in touch with the Hon. Secretary. items.label: March 1939
items.sum: Club notes on Christmas fixtures lost to snow, the Hon. Editor being pulled in a walk, Harry Churcher's walking wins, other clubs' magazines, Belgrave men in the Inter-Counties and a clash of walk dates. Includes a letter of thanks from Tommy Scrimshaw.
e: London Business Houses Road Walking Championship
items.s: This And That. Club notes on Christmas fixtures lost to snow, the Hon. Editor being pulled in a walk, Harry Churcher's walking wins, other clubs' magazines, Belgrave men in the Inter-Counties and a clash of walk dates. Includes a letter of thanks from Tommy Scrimshaw. The Clerk of the Weather has not been any too kind towards our fixture list. By giving us a White Christmas the following races had to be cancelled : Match v. Ealing H. and Metropolitan Police, the Boxing Day Handicaps, and the Croydon-Godstone and back Walk. The latter, as I understand, will be held later on. As regards the match on Christmas Eve, some of the Ealing and Police runners enjoyed a social run with our own lads; the only regret being that they had to soil the virgin snow with their footprints. I'm sure that they will always remember this run whenever they hear that well-known verse of "Good King Wenceslas." * * * * * To the cries of "You ought to go back to running, your Hon. Editor was challenged to place on record the fact that he was "pulled" in the Club "Junior" Championship. Having also been guilty of walking in a running race (Poly Marathon) my perversity would appear to be complete. I take comfort, however, in the knowledge that I must be "pulled" another five times before I can even think of calling myself a walker. * * * * * The appearance in the local press (re our Dance on November 26th), of a question asking whether we needed exercise, might be interpreted to indicate the inadequacy of our training, or that we had taken a leaf from the book of the local "Keep Fit Campaign." To this comment on our activities might be added the fact that many members (don't ask me why !) walked many miles home in the small hours of the morning. At a slightly larger hour they met again. What for? Oh, just for a training stroll! Harry Churcher gained further honours in winning the London Business Houses Road Walking Championship (7 miles). Eddie also gained distinction in this race by being the first man home from the West End Business Houses, thereby earning the crown which once belonged to Percy Wright. * * * * * I have recently had the pleasure of reading the official organs of other Clubs. One was from one of the oldest, "The L.A.C. News." In the three numbers which I perused were detailed reports of their activities, interspersed with articles by such well-known athletes as F. A. R. Hunter, J. E. Lovelock, B. F. McCabe, J. V. Powell and P. D. Ward; whilst there was an article by D. H. A. Christie-Murray on walking. The other was from one of the younger Clubs, "The Southgate Harrier." This gazette only came into existence last year, but it has already attained an excellent standard, and a high degree of enthusiasm supplies the undercurrent to the reports of the sterling performances by their members in matches and club races. I am sure that all readers of the "Belgravian" will wish for its continued success. Both these magazines make very good reading, and I am sure that their readers look forward to each issue. * * * * * In the Inter-Counties Cross Country Championship, held at Harpenden (Herts.) on January 21st, C. T. Carter and A. W. Penny scored in the winning Surrey team. D. Patience and H. W. Shields helped Middlesex to be runners-up, whilst E. S. Stimpson also appeared in the Middlesex team, but was not in the scoring. * * * * * The new date for the Surrey W.C. Croydon-Godstone and back walk, postponed from Boxing Day, is April 22nd. This, unfortunately, coincides with our own twenty miles road-walking championship, so that Belgrave vests will be absent from the Eastbourne road on that day. * * * * * One can quite truthfully say of Harry Churcher that "he takes the cake," for he was awarded a cake by the Editor of the J. Lyons & Co. Sports Sheet. This prize is awarded to the man (or woman) who has the most meritorious sporting performance of the week to their credit. Harry's award was in respect of his win in the Ashcombe-St. George's open race. items.s: 7 Miles C.C. Championship. H. W. Shields's report and full result of the club 7 miles cross-country championship of 10 December 1938, won by C. T. Carter, with the handicap won by J. R. Shotter and Belgrave H. beating Cadogan A.C. on team scores. 10th December, 1938. The long-sought cure for the alleged slow starts of our teams in championships can be said to have been found. Whether it was design or accident has not yet been discovered, but the struggle of Belgrave's manhood for supemacy in the race to a camera some 200 yards down the course could only be described as on a par with the Gold Rush. The office of photographer to the teams should carefully be looked into! Settling down to serious work after this very fast start, Pat Parker forged ahead with Tom Carter, Dan Patience and several others in close attendance. This order was maintained until the hills were reached, when Tom Carter went strongly to the fore, and at the end of the first lap had established a useful lead, with Dan Patience, Charlie Smart and Pat Parker following. This order was maintained to the finish, with the exception of Arthur Penny (who must have done fastest time in the second lap) who beat Parker for 4th place. Congratulations to J. R. Shotter, who closely won the handicap held in conjunction with the championship, from L. Penny. Both of these, with careful training, should prove very useful acquisitions to our future championship teams. Micky Walker obtained 3rd place in the handicap and will, no doubt, get much encouragement from his fine run. Several of our younger members gave sterling accounts of themselves : Beard, Rispin, Shrubb and others, who will prove their worth in later races. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. Pos. Name. items.h: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H.
items.sum: E. A. Duffett's report and result of the junior cross-country match of 31 December against Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. at Belgrave Hall, won by Belgrave with 31 points to Blackheath's 37 though M. W. Jenkins of Blackheath took first place.
e: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H.
items.s: Junior Match v. Blackheath and Old Croydonians H. E. A. Duffett's report and result of the junior cross-country match of 31 December against Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. at Belgrave Hall, won by Belgrave with 31 points to Blackheath's 37 though M. W. Jenkins of Blackheath took first place. On Saturday, December 31st, we had the pleasure of entertaining the Junior members of the Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians H. It was the first time we had met these clubs in a cross-country match and I hope they enjoyed their visit to Belgrave Hall. A field of just under 30 runners faced our President, who acted as starter, but owing to the Old Croydonians being rather short of men, it was decided to score 5 aside. After the usual fast start our boys soon forged to the front, and when they came to the Kingsmere and turned towards the Windmill and home, it was seen that E. H. Herbert was leading, with W. E. Beard next, followed by B. Rowe, who is a newcomer to our ranks. Leading a small bunch of black vests was M. W. Jenkins, of Blackheath, and he displayed fine judgment in moving up to his opponents, so that by the time the runners had passed the Windmill, Herbert only led him by a mere 10 yards. Beard and Rowe were next, but our other men seemed rather a long way back. Jenkins soon had the measure of our lad and eventually ran home an easy winner in quite good time for this course. Herbert was a good second with Beard close behind, and then came Rowe, who had quite surprised us by his form in his first club race. As, however, both the Blackheath H. and Old Croydonians wear black vests, what had seemed at first a most formidable bunch of opponents just behind our boys, turned out to consist of three "Heathens" and two "Old Boys." Thus scoring five aside, we came out narrow winners by the margin of 6 points from Blackheath. We sincerely hope that next season we shall renew our sporting rivalry over the country with our opponents on this occasion. RESULT. Pos. Name Club Time 1 M. W. Jenkins Bkh. 31 31 2 E. H. items.sum: T. C. Jones's report of the Surrey County Senior cross-country championship at Petersham, won by Mitcham from Surrey with Belgrave third and C. T. Carter third individually; the text puts Herbert 28th at half distance while the result lists L. W. Herbert 18.
items.s: Surrey County Senior Championship. T. C. Jones's report of the Surrey County Senior cross-country championship at Petersham, won by Mitcham from Surrey with Belgrave third and C. T. Carter third individually; the text puts Herbert 28th at half distance while the result lists L. W. Herbert 18. The Surrey County Championship was run over the Ranelagh Harriers' course at Petersham this year—a slightly hilly course. Our team was not so strong as in former years, owing to the absence of Footer and Cohen, but we had hopes of at least repeating our performance of last year in finishing second to Mitcham. The draw for positions was not too favourable to us and our boys did not get away too well, Kemp being the only one in the first dozen after about a mile. When the runners were next seen, at about half distance, Carter was in the first three, together with Brown (Mitcham) and Hines (Surrey), with Penny (7th), Kemp (25th), Lucas (27th), Herbert (28th) and Mick Walker (30th) completing our scoring six. Mitcham seemed to be leading Surrey by a few points with ourselves third, and it looked as if we would have to put in a lot of running in the second lap to gain the points required to put us close up to Mitcham and Surrey. About a quarter of a mile from the finish Brown (Mitcham) led, followed by Close (Surrey) about 40 yards behind, who was closely followed by Carter, and so the first three stayed until the finish. A quick check-up of the scores showed that although we had gained a number of points in the last lap, both Mitcham and Surrey had gained points and kept well in front of us. Mitcham eventually ran out winners, to add to their success of last year, but only by a few points from Surrey, with ourselves filling third place. Congratulations to Tom Carter on his excellent showing and to all the rest of the team, and further congratulations to Carter and Penny on being selected to represent the County in the Inter Counties Race. items.s: The Middlesex Cross Country Championship. Report of the Middlesex cross-country championship, in which Belgrave's Middlesex-qualified members ran as Cadogan A.C. and beat Thames Valley Harriers and Polytechnic Harriers, with Ted Stimpson second. In this event our members who possess qualifications for this County ran for Cadogan A.C. Although they were without the assistance of J. C. Smart, A. E. Taylor and H. G. Verney, they scored a convincing win over Thames Valley Harriers and Polytechnic Harriers, who were much fancied by the newspaper prophets to win easily. Ted Stimpson gave a first-class performance to finish second individual. The rest of our team packed very well—D. Patience was 4th, H. W. Shields 7th, A. Allum 14th, R. Tobin 15th and F. R. Webb 17th. The next Cadogan man home was A. Smith, who gave one of the best performances of his career to finish 58th. Although just missing inclusion in the scoring six, Bert can claim satisfaction in the knowledge that had his performance been required for the team, they would still have won. Another feature of our win was the fine running, on a very heavy course, of two veterans, A. Allum and F. R. Webb. J. Daly was Cadogan's only other representative in this race and, no doubt, he was as pleased with carrying the colours of a winning team as though he were one of the scorers! He finished 96th. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's convincing team win (27 pts.) in the Surrey Junior cross-country championship on Wimbledon Common from the club headquarters, led home by E. H. Herbert in fourth, ahead of Surrey A.C., with Surrey Beagles and Mitcham A.C. tied third.
items.s: The Surrey Junior Cross-Country Championship. Report of Belgrave's convincing team win (27 pts.) in the Surrey Junior cross-country championship on Wimbledon Common from the club headquarters, led home by E. H. Herbert in fourth, ahead of Surrey A.C., with Surrey Beagles and Mitcham A.C. tied third. Our Juniors scored a most convincing win in this race, which was held from our own headquarters. They had the advantage of knowing the country, but the margin of their win outweighs any suggestion of "Horses for Courses." With the exception of F. S. Bradnum, who unfortunately had to drop out, they showed good packing and team work, as can be seen by glancing at their finishing positions. It was hard luck indeed that Bradnum was unable to give his usual sound performance. The fact that they excelled themselves in a Championship race shows that they have been training wisely. The day was rather muggy, and a large crowd of young runners started out on their tour of Wimbledon Common. Our lads soon found themselves in useful positions and our hopes were fairly bright when they left for the open country. E. H. Herbert led our lads home, finishing in fourth position, thus confirming the good form which he has been showing. Lionel Penny proved his consistency by finishing eighth, one place ahead of another promising runner, W. E. Beard. Len Marchant, 15th, completed the scoring four. To these four lads we give our heartiest congratulations on their well-earned honours. Our non-scoring men, R. Boyden 18th, J. R. Shotter 23rd, N. C. Shrubb 24th, have every reason to be pleased with themselves; for having the non-scoring men well placed adds relish to our win. R. V. Reynolds ran as an individual and finished 36th. Our Juniors can well be proud of themselves for doing their bit in upholding the Club's prestige. The Club, in turn, is proud of them and hopes to see them graduate to further honours. items.h: "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship."
items.sum: Ubiquitor's humorous account and full result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship of 28 January 1939, in which Arthur Penny retained his title after a close struggle with Tom Carter and G. Murdock won the handicap.
items.s: "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship." Ubiquitor's humorous account and full result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship of 28 January 1939, in which Arthur Penny retained his title after a close struggle with Tom Carter and G. Murdock won the handicap. "A Fight to the Death" or "Through Mud to Glory" or "The 10 Mile Championship." On Saturday, 28th January, the Club 10 Miles Championship resulted in Arthur Penny retaining his title after one of the best struggles that we have seen in a race famous for its keen struggles. The field was almost the smallest for several years, there being notable absentees, including Bert Footer. As usual, they started over the circuit of the field at a cracking pace, all in a bunch with Ted Stimpson, Penny and Harry Shields leading, but by the time they were back at the start (1 mile) there were three distinct packs with six in the fast, eight in the medium and I lost count of the slow. But half a mile later across the golf links they had to "paddle" a small lake (to the amusement of the spectators, but not the runners) and here Arthur Penny, with a determined expression, moved away from the others with Tom Carter hard on his heels. These two set a fast pace through the woods, and up the hockey field they had a lead of 25 yards from Stimpson, Shields and Dan. The sixth of the original fast pack, Jerman, was back another 50 yards with Tobin, Arthur Allum, and Murdock, on his heels. But the rest were already well spread out, breathing hard, some looking distressed, and it was here that I saw Jimmy Kemp collecting rude answers by standing on one side and telling everyone: "Only another 7½ miles!" Up to the pond Penny eased off a bit and seemed to be having a bad time and Carter took up the running, but he was unable to get away, and at half distance he led by a yard from Penny, with Stimpson 100 yards back, Dan another 50, and Harry tagging on behind. There was a gap of 150 yards before Allum came along just ahead of Jerman, Mick Walker and Alf Shaw, with Murdock and Tobin just behind. At this point I was pleased to notice the fine style and high position of "Champ" Smith. The waterlogged course was taking toll, and several dropped out here (ya yeller!), but Tom and Arthur went on relentlessly fighting each other across the golf course and its lake (very funny!) and they went down through the "forest" at a terrible pace, Tom trying desperately to get a lead. They were now well over 200 yards ahead of Stimpson, who had now been challenged by Dan Patience. Harry Shields was another 70 yards away and no one else was in sight. Going much slower up the hockey field, Tom still had his yard lead, but both looked whacked to the wide and were only going by will power. They stayed the same up to the pond, where Arthur made his supreme effort and burst away into a lead of 40 yards, which he held home. Neither had anything left and the time is a true testimony of their splendid efforts. Meanwhile Dan led Stimpson up the hockey field, fell 70 yards behind going up the hill, caught it up and was leading again half a mile from home; but he was unable to hold his gallant effort to the finish. Over the last mile they were both catching up on the leaders, although they finished over a minute behind Penny. Shields pounded along by himself and finished strongly, Mick Walker did well to finish 6th and Murdock is to be congratulated on a very good performance and his first handicap win in the club. While we are presenting bouquets, a special word of praise is due to Messrs. Stride (12) and Boyden (14), who showed splendid promise on graduating from the junior section. Good luck to them both; and a special word for George Still, who at 62 can cover ten miles at what seems to us a phenomenal pace—we expect him to win the race when he has had a little more experience! Finally, the handicapper did his usual fine bit of work—but don't tell him I said so, he knows it already! RESULT. Pos. Name Act Time Start H'c'p Time Pos. in H'c'p 1 A. W. items.sum: Report and result of the club 5 miles junior cross-country championship for the "Savage" Shield at Wimbledon on 28 January 1939, won by E. H. Herbert from L. K. Penny.
items.s: Club Junior C.C. Championship. Report and result of the club 5 miles junior cross-country championship for the "Savage" Shield at Wimbledon on 28 January 1939, won by E. H. Herbert from L. K. Penny. On Saturday, January 28th, at Wimbledon, we held the Club 5 miles Junior C.C. Championship for the "Savage" Shield. We were sorry the donor was not able to be with us owing to illness, and we take this opportunity of wishing him a speedy recovery to good health. Last year's holder was now too old to compete, owing to the age limit of 21 for this race, and a dozen Juniors faced the starter, each keen to be the one to annex the trophy. Lionel Penny led the field along at a fast pace over the first small lap and was still leading when they went out into the country. A small bunch, which included Beard and Herbert, had settled down some 30 to 40 yards in the rear, and in the long steady pull up to the Kingsmere, Herbert put in some telling work to overhaul the leader. On the run home via the Windmill, Herbert had now taken command of the race and was some 50 yards in front of Penny, with Beard about 30 yards behind the second man. At this point Shotter was putting in some very strong running but had left his effort rather too late, while Edwards and Shrubb were also running well. Marchant was not reproducing his Surrey Junior form but in view of his age this runner has many years left in which to win this race. We were sorry that B. Rowe, our young runner at Glasgow University, was unable to be present, while we must also congratulate J. McDonald on his plucky running after going off the course at one stage of the race. items.sum: H. Parker's report and result of the juniors' cross-country match against the Guards Depot at Caterham on 4 February 1939, won by newcomer W. Hewitt, with Belgrave winning the eight-a-side team race 69-76.
items.s: Match v. Guards Depot (Caterham). H. Parker's report and result of the juniors' cross-country match against the Guards Depot at Caterham on 4 February 1939, won by newcomer W. Hewitt, with Belgrave winning the eight-a-side team race 69-76. On Saturday, February 4th, an enthusiastic party of Juniors journeyed to Caterham to meet the Guards Depot in an inter-team contest. All were optimistic as to what the result would be, although the strength of the Depot was an unknown quantity. Our spirits were a little damped when the Sergeant Major told us that the course was a tough one. It was both hilly and heavy, two of our lads losing their shoes, whilst another arrived home carrying one! Afterwards they all agreed that they had had an enjoyable race! A newcomer to most of us, but one who has already made a name for himself in the North, W. Hewitt, ran home a very comfortable winner. We hope that he will carry our colours right to the front in the South. His time for the five miles was 33 min. 52 sec. Lionel Penny was the next to arrive in 34 min. 30 sec., followed by the first soldier, Sgt. Nelson, in 34 min. 40 sec. N. Shrubb was fourth, R. Boyden sixth, L. Marchant eighth, R. Johnson ninth, B. Martin fourteenth, A. T. A. Jordan twenty-fifth, J. Daly twenty-sixth, and P Stevenson, a newcomer from Glasgow, who lost both the way home and his shoes! completed our little band. The result of the team race, scoring eight aside, went in our favour 69—76. We have to thank the soldiers for the very splendid tea with which they provided us; but what was most appreciated was the MUG of hot tea which was awaiting the runners at the finish of the race. items.h: The South of Thames Senior, Royal Military College, Sandhurst.
items.sum: Ubiquitor's report and our men's result in the South of Thames senior cross-country race at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, on 10 February 1939, won by T. A. Cattell, with Blackheath first team and an under-strength Belgrave sixth of 23 teams.
items.s: The South of Thames Senior, Royal Military College, Sandhurst. Ubiquitor's report and our men's result in the South of Thames senior cross-country race at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, on 10 February 1939, won by T. A. Cattell, with Blackheath first team and an under-strength Belgrave sixth of 23 teams. 10th February, 1939. R. I. P. When I first saw our team I thought that it looked quite promising, but when I found that Jerman had hurt his eyes (fortunately only temporarily) and could not run, that Kemp had a gammy hip, that Tommy Morrell was convalescent and that E. Herbert was not fit, I did not think it quite so good! Bels. were well drawn for once and Kemp made a clean start and the large field went away over the first lap round the very charming College Field (1 mile), and as they went by we had quite a few lying well up: Murdock 12, Tobin 20, Kemp 26, and E. Herbert 30, with brother Herbert not far away. Three-quarters of a mile later, when the runners disappeared into the wood, the position had not greatly changed, for Murdock was 13th, Tobin 18th, Kemp 26th, and although E. Herbert had dropped to 65th, Stride was running really well and had come up to 40th. After Herbert there was quite a patch of claret and gold. Johnson and L. Herbert were together 74 and 75, and another group of Messrs. Boyden, Smith and Rispin 84—86, while Mitchell at 112 was just two places ahead of Tommy Morrell. The course on the big lap was hilly, rather sandy, and loose in places, but quite dry, and the leaders began to go away from the rest of the field. I am afraid that some of our leaders lost a few places here, and half-way round the lap Kemp was our first man in 22nd, Tobin 23, Murdock 43, and then the rest of the team all within striking distance of one another. It was here that there was a steepish hill (ask the runners!) which I believe caught Kemp's hip rather badly, for he began to lose ground, but Murdock passed both Tobin and Kemp and made up several places. At the end of the first big lap the positions were: Murdock 19, Tobin 24, Kemp 32, Stride 46, E. (Young) Herbert going steadily at 71st, then a little pack having a friendly fight, Johnson 80, L. Herbert 81, Boyden 85, Champ Smith 86, and Rispin 87, with Mitchell still just ahead of Morrell a little further back. There was little alteration in positions over the second lap in the country, except for the steady dropping of Kemp, who was caught and passed by Stride at the top of the hill, but I did notice that the junior members of the team were running very steadily, and show promise of doing well, with a little more time and experience. Coming back on to the sports field, with only three-quarters of a mile to go, Murdock was 18th, Tobin 19th, Stride had run through to 37th, but looked rather tired, while Kemp was back at 54 and the brothers Herbert, L. and E., were 72 and 75. Our friendly pack all seemed to have decided that they had run together far enough, but as they all tried to get away from one another at the same time they were not very successful. Moral: start earlier next time! We were not in danger of being one of the first three teams, which was fortunate, as we lost several useful places over that last lap, as can be seen from the positions below. We did not even get the "12" shield for the first club to finish twelve men, usually a strong point with us, so it was perhaps a little disappointing, but I am sure that had we had a complete and fit team we should have had much more to sing about. RESULT. TEAM SCORES. 23 teams closed in. We are greatly indebted to Bill Sutton, whose details of placings during the race were most helpful. The conditions were excellent for running and the afternoon was warm, bright and sunny, and we, the spectators, had a very good time, with a pleasant coach journey through a beautiful part of Surrey for the moderate fare of 2/3. Why don't a few more people treat themselves to a really good afternoon to give the lads a cheer? m. s. 1 T. A. Cattell (S.L.H.) 46 22 2 G. Lucas (G. & D.) 46 43 3 R. F. Towndrow (Ash.) 47 9 19 G. items.sum: Report and result of the Belgrave Open Walk of 26 November 1938, won by Harry Churcher in a course record from E. A. Staker, with Belgrave's C and A teams first and second in the scratch team race.
items.s: The Belgrave Open Walk. Report and result of the Belgrave Open Walk of 26 November 1938, won by Harry Churcher in a course record from E. A. Staker, with Belgrave's C and A teams first and second in the scratch team race. 26th November, 1938. By knocking 43 seconds off the course record (held by V. W. G. Stone, Poly), Harry Churcher treated a large crowd of onlookers to an excellent display of fast walking and his fellow-competitors to a clean pair of heels. At a signal from our President, 176 walkers sped up Lauriston Road. The judges soon got to work, for Colin Sutton was disqualified when he had only covered about a quarter of a mile. After a small lap of the Common, Harry was already in front, and Belgrave vests were already prominent. At the half-way stage it became evident that, barring accidents, Belgrave were due for a lion's share of the prizes; for our men who were prominent at the start maintained their positions. Harry eventually won from E. A. Staker (Highgate H.) by the comfortable margin of 1 min. 30 secs. Joe Coleman gave us his usual sound performance to fill third place, whilst Percy Wright walked hard all the way to finish fifth. The performances of the rest of our lads can best be shown by looking at the team results. In the scratch team results a preliminary word of explanation is necessary. Our A and C teams (captain's and vice-captain's) were chosen from our best men, and, on paper, there appeared little to choose between them. The chances of the A team were weakened by the disqualifications of Sutton and Treacher. This caused them to have to go into the forties for their fourth man—Stan Goold, who, by the way, is performing well this season. Thus handicapped, they were beaten by the C team, but they were worthy runners-up. To finish two scratch teams first and second in an open race (22 teams taking part) and having accomplished this with two men ruled out, speaks volumes for our present strength. Our B team were only a few points behind the A team, and occupied fifth posiition; that is, only two other clubs could beat our third team. Looking at the handicap section, it was no great surprise to find that our B team had returned the lowest aggregate time. The individual handicap prize went to the Highgate Centurion, A. D. McSweeney. Charlie Churcher won the special prize awarded to the first Belgrave Harrier not gaining any other award. The special prize for Police competitors was won by the man who won it last year—R. C. Aylen. This account would be incomplete without recording our most sincere thanks to the following: Messrs. T. Askew, C. E. Churcher, F. H. Elson and E. Gordon for their donations to the prize fund; also to W. Allen, who provided a special prize. Then there is our indebtedness to the R.W.A. officials and handicappers, the local police and the many Club members who acted as pointsmen. Lastly, to those Clubs and Individuals who supported the event and helped to make it the success which deservedly rewarded the efforts of those responsible for its organisation. items.sum: Report and result of the club seven mile "junior" walk for the Horwood Cup on 17 December 1938, won by Bert Clayton from Eddie Heather and Syd Roberts, with Frank Jarvis winning the sealed handicap.
items.s: The Seven Mile "Junior" Walk. Report and result of the club seven mile "junior" walk for the Horwood Cup on 17 December 1938, won by Bert Clayton from Eddie Heather and Syd Roberts, with Frank Jarvis winning the sealed handicap. Saturday, 17th December, 1938. This race for the Horwood Cup was held a week later than was originally arranged, and fourteen walkers shivered in Lauriston Road, waiting for the word to start from Oscar Horwood. Bert Clayton immediately went into the lead, accompanied by Bert East, with Syd Roberts leading the rest in pursuit. After a small lap of the Common, Clayton was still leading, Eddie Heather having worked his way into second place. These two were still leading at the top of the hills, with Roberts leading Thaxter and Doubleday for third place. Going round the common again, Heather was a few yards in front, but there was little to choose between them when the hills were tackled again. Roberts seemed to be moving better now and appeared to be gaining on his rivals. Coming up the hills the second time Clayton, after a ding-dong battle, had gained a lead of twenty yards or so, but Heather stuck gamely to his task, and finally had to admit defeat after a most thrilling race. Roberts maintained his position and was a worthy third. Harry Thaxter gave an excellent performance to finish fourth. Clayton's victory bears out the form which he has shown in open races this season. It is a fitting reward for his keenness, for, living at Eastleigh, he has not had the advantage of training with a pack. He is, however, under the watchful eye of Tommy Green, to whom, no doubt, his success will be a source of satisfaction. The performances of the others will assure the Club that our reserve talent will become worthy successors to the traditions set by our teams. L. Little, one of this season's newcomers, shows continued improvement, whilst W. F. Brunning progresses steadily and will perform better over the longer distances. Frank Jarvis won the sealed handicap, and our old friend, Bill Snell, worked his way into second place. A comparative newcomer, W. H. Jones, gave evidence of his prowess by claiming third place. No doubt this will be a great encouragement to him, and his improvement will continue. The race was slightly marred by the absence of Bridger, Elliott and Speechley, whose presence would most certainly have made the race keener. RESULT. Pos. Name Act. Time Allce. items.s: The London Transport Open Walk. Report and result of the London Transport Open Walk on 4 February 1939, won by Harry Churcher, with Belgrave winning the scratch team race and the B team second in the handicap team race. 4th February, 1939. This event is usually a bogey race for our men, as many of them manage to get "pulled." This year's race was no exception, for only a bare four of our "A" team got through to complete the course. The course, which is aptly described as two and a half laps of housing estate and gasworks, would appear to be, judging from the times returned, a good seven miles. The walkers were pleased to find that the steepest hill on the course, a narrow lane with muddy banks on each side, had been modernised to form a wide concrete "speedway." This appeared to render the hill a little less formidable. The usual men soon found their way to the front, and by the time that the headquarters were reached (after about a mile) Harry Churcher was at the head of a well strung out field. On the first of the two large laps came catastrophe number one. Charlie Churcher, after having steadily worked his way into a useful position, suffered disqualification. Alan Bridger and Bill Treacher also shared a similar fate. This reduced our "A" team to four (seven only starting). A quick reckoning by our Walking Hon. Sec. made us potential winners of the scratch team race, so he gave our men a timely warning to watch their step. Harry was first home exactly two minutes ahead of his nearest rival, H. H. Whitlock (Metropolitan W.C.), who must have given some of the short distance specialists a shock. Joe Coleman was fourth, whilst Percy Wright and Len Coleman completed the team. Our "B" team (Clark, Doubleday, Roberts and True) managed to get in the prize-winners again, taking second handicap team prize. Brunning, Jones and Little also gave us encouraging performances, and their constant support of open races is an excellent testimony to their keenness and club-spirit. RESULT. items.sum: Report and result of the club Ten Miles walking championship on 28 January 1939, won by Harry Churcher from his brother Charlie and Joe Coleman, with Belgrave also beating the Met. Police W.C. in a match held in conjunction.
items.s: The Ten Miles Championship. Report and result of the club Ten Miles walking championship on 28 January 1939, won by Harry Churcher from his brother Charlie and Joe Coleman, with Belgrave also beating the Met. Police W.C. in a match held in conjunction. Saturday, 28th January, 1939. An ex-holder of this Championship, Harold King, started a large field of walkers, which included members of the M.P.A.A. and Surrey A.C. Three men immediately shot to the front—Harry Churcher and the Coleman brothers. After two laps of the Common, Harry already had a good lead, whilst his brother Charlie, after a modest start, had now got well into his stride and was close on the heels of Percy Wright, who then occupied fourth position. Out to Roehampton and back there were many private "dust-ups," and on reaching the War Memorial there were many who wished that the race finished at Lauriston Road. But, alas, there were two laps of the Common to be done. By this time the cold was beginning to take its toll and some gave it best and retired. On his final lap of the Common, Harry Churcher got a view of some of his fellow-competitors—they were still struggling on the first of their two laps. This meant that he was a mile in front of them! Brother Charlie showed a welcome return to form by finishing second, Joe Coleman being third. When the handicap result was announced, the name of Churcher was again at the head, for not only did Harry win from scratch (he's done that before!) but Charlie's efforts were rewarded with second prize. Alan Bridger, who is now finding his form after a slight setback in the shape of a bad leg, followed by a cold, was a worthy third. We were again successful in our match v. the M.P.A.A., which was held in conjunction, and the usual practice of having our Police members scoring for the "boys in blue" was adhered to. RESULT. Pos. items.s: The Ashcombe-St. George's Open Walk. Report and result of the Ashcombe-St. George's Open Walk on 21 January 1939, won by Harry Churcher, with Belgrave winning the scratch team race and so retaining the R.W.A. Berman Cup. 21st January, 1939. There was added interest in this race this year as the R.W.A. "Berman" Cup was awarded in conjunction with the scratch race. The day was very muggy, and some hundred odd competitors, after many almost bewildering left and right turns, found themselves in Richmond Park. As can be well imagined, there were some small ups and downs, but no severe gradients, the tendency of the course being uphill on the outward journey and downhill coming home. It was very pleasing to see some of our runners in the Park, and their vocal encouragements were both welcome and much appreciated. Harry Churcher recorded his customary win, Vic Stone (Poly) beating E. Staker (Highgate) for second place. Another Poly man, H. D. Neilson, was fourth. Joe Coleman and Charlie Churcher were fifth and sixth, the latter having made a moderate start, his position improving as the race progressed. Our Junior Champion, Bert Clayton, was tenth to complete the team; his getting into the scoring four was as popular as it was well-merited. Thus we retained the Berman Cup and, whilst we cheer the men who won it, we must not forget to add a word of congratulation to Harry Thaxter, who gained third prize in the handicap. RESULT. items.h: The Valentine's S.C. Open Ten Miles Walk.
items.sum: Report and result of the Valentine's S.C. Open Ten Miles Walk at Goodmayes on 18 February 1939, won by D. Christie-Murray, with Belgrave's A team winning the scratch team race in Harry Churcher's absence and the B team second in the handicap team race.
e: Valentine's S.C. Open Ten Miles Walk
items.s: The Valentine's S.C. Open Ten Miles Walk. Report and result of the Valentine's S.C. Open Ten Miles Walk at Goodmayes on 18 February 1939, won by D. Christie-Murray, with Belgrave's A team winning the scratch team race in Harry Churcher's absence and the B team second in the handicap team race. This race was held on February 18th, in the Goodmayes neighbourhood, and attracted a large entry, including 22 Belgravians. This is the only ten miles open handicap of the season, and we had high hopes of maintaining our sequence of scratch team race wins in open events. The news that Harry Churcher, hero of a dozen or more successive Open race wins, was prevented from turning out owing to a bout of influenza was disappointing, and the fact that Percy Wright was recovering from similar trouble, seemed to make scratch team prospects more open than has been the case in recent races. Both Metropolitan Walking Club and Surrey Walking Club seemed to be at full strength and we anticipated a keen struggle with both these old-standing rivals. The brothers Coleman and E. A. Staker led the field at the start, until Len found the pace a little too warm and dropped back. Mile after mile Joe Coleman and Highgate's E. A. Staker kept shoulder to shoulder in the lead, until about six miles or more, when D. Christie Murray, of Surrey W.C., came through the field with a determined and extraordinarily well-judged turn of speed. Staker attempted to go after him, but later had the mortification of slipping back to eighth position. Meanwhile, Harold Whitlock had been gaining places and eventually beat our Joe by a small margin. An attempt to total the team scores at six miles (approx.) showed that we were scoring 35 points to the 36 of the Metropolitan W.C.! Whitlock, of the Met., appeared likely to gain places and it will be realized that excitement reigned. Our boys were apprised of the facts and immediately responded. Joe Coleman was determined to finish well up. Colin Sutton set about gaining places, as did also our Captain, Charlie Churcher. Len Coleman, fourth "A" team man, also moved up, and Eddie Heather, of the "B" team, and Bert Clayton, fifth and non-scoring "A" team man, rendered yeoman service. They were told to overtake the Metropolitan men and right well they set about their task. The position improved and at eight miles approximately we were leading with 30 points to the 42 of Metropolitan W.C., whilst Surrey Walking Club were also improving their position. Still, our walkers gained places, and their determination was grand to see, and a tribute to their loyalty to their Club and team-mates. At the finish we were comparatively easy winners, and whilst the efforts of our scoring four were splendidly maintained and worthy of the highest praise, they will be eager to join in the tribute to Clayton and Heather. Unable to score in the team themselves, these two did marvellous work in pushing the other clubs back; and displayed team spirit at its very highest level. May both receive the reward merited in the "Junior" Championship, which follows a fortnight later! While our six aforementioned men were finishing in the first twelve places, our other walkers were also striving hard and with some effect. Messrs. Roberts, Doubleday, Clark and Heather, of the "B" team, walked well and comprised the second handicap team. Eddie Heather's forward walking, his best to date, earned third individual handicap prize. All things considered, we can look back with a deal of pleasure on this event. We regretted the absence of Harry Churcher from our team, but it was pleasing to find that we had others in plenty to give of their best and make up for his absence. RESULT. E. C. items.label: March 1939
items.sum: Walking column on the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship win (the club's seventh), the coming walking fixtures and training, a call for new walkers, and an appeal to join the Road Walking Association as individual members.
items.s: With The Walkers. Walking column on the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship win (the club's seventh), the coming walking fixtures and training, a call for new walkers, and an appeal to join the Road Walking Association as individual members. So we have won the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship once again. A full account must follow in our next issue, but we heartily congratulate the team responsible for our seventh win in this series of races. No other club can approach this record of success, the next best being the four wins of Surrey Walking Club. As we won last year's race (with a record score) and this team was no longer eligible, we were set the task of finding four new scoring men. This we succeeded in doing, and two successive wins is of the greatest credit to all concerned. Next year we shall be out to put up a "best-ever" performance and score another win. It must be admitted that this presents many difficulties We have some very fine young walkers coming along but they will probably not be sufficiently matured in time for next March. So we shall, in all probability, rely upon this year's candidates for places in our team, plus the new members that we hope will be forthcoming during the next few months. We trust that all members will keep a keen look-out for new talent, and we can assure all who join the ranks of the walkers a cordial welcome, good times, and a guaranteed measure of success if they are prepared to persevere. * * * * * Now for the "Senior," to be held on May 13th from the Police quarters at Hendon. As the title-holders, we shall use all our endeavours to hold on to the Championship. It would be a wonderful feat to win once again all three "R.W.A." titles in one season, and one which is within our capabilities. * * * * * We hope to have all last year's men again representing us, supplemented by some of those who have now left the "Junior" ranks behind for ever. The Club Championship at 20 miles, with sealed handicap in conjunction, will be held at Wimbledon on April 22nd. The Metropolitan Police W.C. and Surrey A.C. will also be visitors. It is unfortunate that the postponed "Godstone" Walk is to be held on the same day, but our S.W.C. friends realise that we have to carry through with our arrangements. * * * * * The following Saturday we expect to travel eastwards for the Colchester to Ipswich Walk, won by Colin Sutton last year. * * * * * The R.W.A. 50 kilos Championship is to be held from De Bohun's Farm, Southgate, on July 22nd. This is another title to be defended and we have every confidence in our men. With the Olympic Games to follow in 1940, we shall be looking to this Championship event to give us some guide as to England's representatives the following year. * * * * * Our Inter-club scratch Walks will be held at Battersea Park Track on Wednesday, May 31st, when we expect to receive the usual very fine support of clubs in the Metropolitan area. * * * * * We should like to add twenty new walkers to our ranks during the Summer months. The Hon. Secretary, Track Captain, and other officials will do all in their power to assist the newcomer to walking and put him on his way to success. All enquiries and entries should be addressed to— A. A. Harley, 39, Roxborough Avenue, Isleworth, Mx. * * * * * Training for the Track Walking season will take place on Tuesday evenings at Battersea Park, commencing when the clocks are adjusted to Summer time. Any member, especially the newer ones, who require further particulars, should write to the Track Captain, P. G. Wright, 23, Campana Road, S.W.6, who will gladly give any information needed. The Road Walking Association has, in recent years, found it very difficult to function at its highest point of efficiency, by reason of its limited finances. The only income the Association receives is in the form of 25% of the affiliation fees paid by Clubs to the District Associations, and any profits that may be made on the three Championships promoted. It is obvious that with no "gate" to call upon, the Championships are more likely to show a loss than a profit, and so it becomes increasingly difficult to carry on if further progress is to be made. Accordingly, an appeal is made to those interested in road walking to join the Road Walking Association as indvidual members at an annual subscription of 5/-. There is no desire on the part of the Association to bring about any diminution of support by members to their clubs, but it is thought that those who can afford to do so will welcome the chance to assist the Association's finances by enrolling as Honorary Members. Any Belgrave member desirous of so doing is asked to get into touch with A. A. Harley. Colin Sutton Colin Sutton won the Colchester to Ipswich Walk last year A. A. Harley A. A. items.sum: Look back to 1929: Belgrave's first South of the Thames cross-country title, the Southern and National championships, second place in the R.W.A. "Junior" walk, and club news of that year.
e: South of the Thames Cross-country Championship
items.s: Ten Years Back. Look back to 1929: Belgrave's first South of the Thames cross-country title, the Southern and National championships, second place in the R.W.A. "Junior" walk, and club news of that year. The Championship season of 1929 provided us with a great success. For the first time we succeeded in winning the South of the Thames Cross-country Championship, and also the "Colman" Cup as the first club to finish its complete team of twelve men. It was certainly a proud moment for W. H. Hare, the first Belgravian to be President of the South of the Thames Association; and all other Club members present, when the trophies were awarded. Our winning team consisted of W. S. Mitchell (4), A. W. Penny (7), A. Allum (13), W. G. Webb (16), P. Khlopin (23), A. Robertshaw (26), giving us a total of 89 points. Herne Hill Harriers were second with 139 points, and Horsham Blue Star A.C. third with 211 points. The other members of our team were A. E. Smith (44), K. B. O'Kell (56), W. A. Rice (66), A. G. Jones (87), W. L. Bayliss (116), and S. Drake (144). With this first "Senior" Championship win to encourage us, we went hopefully to the "Southern" held at Horton Kirby, but could only finish tenth of the 29 clubs that started. A fortnight later, in the "National" held at Beaconsfield in brilliant sunny weather, our team did not close in. Only four of our runners finished : W. G. Webb (87), A. W. Penny (120), W. L. Bayliss (122) and F. G. Ford (197). Turning to the walking side we find that we were placed second in the R.W.A. "Junior" Championship held at Birmingham in 1929. Surrey W.C. were the winners, and our team consisted of J. E. Field (9), J. Rathbone (11), E. Saunders (13) and F. H. Elson (18). Three members of this team were destined to be in the winning team the following year; and Jack Rathbone was in our winning "Senior" team later in the season. The Southern Amateur Athletic League had just been formed and its first fixture list announced. Our Field Events men were doing their utmost to arouse more interest and enthusiasm, and the conditions to decide the first holder of the "Harry Wright" Shield appear in the April, 1929, issue of "The Belgravian"—the first to be published under the editorship of A. A. Harley. These were the happenings of our Club life ten years ago! W. H. Hare W. H. Hare first Belgravian to be President of the South of the Thames Association W. S. Mitchell W. S. items.label: March 1939
items.sum: Survey of Belgrave athletes with a chance of selection for the 1940 Olympic Games at Helsingfors, event by event from the sprints to the field events and walks, with a summary of Percy Wright's article "Which Walkers for Finland?" and an editor's note.
items.s: Helsingfors, 1940. Survey of Belgrave athletes with a chance of selection for the 1940 Olympic Games at Helsingfors, event by event from the sprints to the field events and walks, with a summary of Percy Wright's article "Which Walkers for Finland?" and an editor's note. The next Olympiad is due to be held in Finland next year, and those athletes who entertain hopes of inclusion in the British team are already planning their training. What are Belgrave's chances of having some of its members in the team? On current form, and with no unlucky breaks, we have many potentialities, and this brief analysis of our own members is intended to give a few ideas as to who may be honoured with selection for the team. In the sprints, S. C. Botwright's name stands out; he also does a very good "quarter." Our other sprinters, judging by last season's results, are on the up-grade, and if some can clip off a few tenths of a second, they will be attracting the selectors' eyes. H. E. Pack has already gained representative honours in the 440 yards, although his times are apt to be dimmed by the performances of A. G. K. Brown and W. Roberts. Our man, however, has beaten 50 seconds on several occasions, recording times which would have won an A.A.A. championship in many years, and if only Eddie could find a sustained finishing effort I am sure we have a world-beater in our ranks. In the 880 yards, A. A. Bird is already inside two minutes, and with a little more age and experience will be doing better. Another man to watch over these distances is S. Jarlett, who last year showed great improvement. We must not, of course, forget T. H. Scrimshaw, who in his day was one of the leading half-milers in the country. Whether Tommy can recover his old form remains to be seen, but I am sure we all wish him the very best of luck. In the 1500 metres, L. W. Herbert and W. E. Lucas are our best, and although neither has yet beaten 4.20 for the Mile, they cannot be overlooked. Lucas gained inclusion in last year's A.A.A. Mile final, while Herbert also gained an A.A.A. standard by beating 4.25. Both of these runners are yet young, and we look forward to still better performances from them both during the coming track season. We have to turn to our cross country men for the 5,000 and 10,000 metres (3 and 6 miles roughly). For the shorter race, C. T. Carter, J. Parker, J. C. Smart and L. J. Cohen can all give good acccounts of themselves, and if only Pat would get down to some serious training, I am sure he could make the team. For the longer race A. W. Penny, an ex-Empire Games 6 miles champion, is still a strong candidate, and although just failing to make the team at the last Olympic Games, we wish him better luck for 1940. D. Patience, S. T. Ring and E. S. Stimpson are three more who do well at these distances, and the latter, an ex-Southern Junior C.C. Champion, is particularly promising and should have a good season. Both having well beaten three hours, A. F. Mitchell and F. A. Walker are well in the running for honours in that classic race—the Marathon; whilst if H. E. Footer should train for the distance—as is probable—he might well win this event for Gt. Britain. For the Steeplechase (3,000 metres) we naturally think of J. Ginty, who was Belgrave's only representative in 1936, but whether Jim's duties will permit of him giving time to the necessary training is rather doubtful. Two others who shine at this branch of athletics are C. T. Carter and A. R. Shaw, and both have good performances to their credit. As regards the Hurdle races, it must be confessed that our chances are extremely remote, the ordinary clubs seem to be rather overshadowed by the Universities and Services in these events, due in the main to lack of training facilities. At the last Olympiad, Great Britain sent very few Field Events competitors, as the performances by Britishers are lamentably below the standards of most other countries. Whether they adopt this procedure again remains to be seen, although we are glad to see that the ruling body have taken steps to encourage this side of athletics among the clubs. Naturally our own club performers are below International standards, but I think that our men deserve attention. That our Field Events section is one of the strongest is evidenced by our performances in the S.A.A.L. Field Events League. In the Shot and Discus, S. Jones, W. H. J. Sutton and L. J. Worrad form a powerful trio who gain us many points in Club matches. In the Javelin, E. H. Finneron, C. A. Melchior, G. H. Powell and Ron Jeal are a useful quartet, whilst our Club champion, H. M. Quackenbos, with more strength and experience, will throw further. For the High and Pole Jumps, our Northern member, J. Dodd, who won the A.A.A. Pole Vault title in 1937, would already have gained International honours but for the fact that he is barred by tht International rules. F. J. Skelley is certainly a bright hope for the Long Jump, he has already cleared 22ft. 8in. and will undoubtedly profit by maturer years. Our Field Events men have been training under F. Stampfl during the Winter, and their performance next Summer will be watched with hope and interest by all. Coming to the Walkers, it is noted that a 10,000 metres walk is planned. For this we have many members who give good accounts of themselves over seven miles. On the form which he has shown in the "Open" races, H. G. Churcher is undoubtedly selection number one, whilst D. E. Brown, C. E. Churcher, H. G. Clayton, J. G. and L. J. Coleman and P. G. Wright are names usually prominent in "Open" races. In the 50 kilometres (31¼ miles) walk, F. E. Bentley, J. C. Bidgood, F. Rickards and C. F. Sutton are strong candidates. Bentley has already represented Great Britain in the European Championships, whilst Sutton was selected as a reserve. At the last Olympiad the only Britisher to win an Individual Championship was H. H. Whitlock in the 50 kilometres walk; whilst in the 1932 Games our own T. W. Green was victorious, and I am sure that if Britain wins this event through a Belgrave Harrier, Tommy will be as pleased (if not more) as all of us. No doubt there are some names which may catch the selectors' eyes which have not been mentioned. These are the members who, by their efforts and enthusiasm will better their past performances. Who are they to be? * * * * * Since writing the above I have received an article from Percy Wright entitled "Which Walkers for Finland?" Economy of space prevents its appearance in full, but here is a brief summary. It deals with the 10,000 metres walk only, and the hope is expressed that the maximum possible number of men will be sent. H. G. Churcher is the first name mentioned, and his classic race with Mikaelsson (Sweden) in 1937 (when Harry returned the fastest time done by an Englishman in the Championships) is cited as proof of his ability on the track. The distance may prove too far for A. A. Cooper (Woodford Green), who has held the two miles championship for several years. F. J. Redman (Metropolitan W.C.) may now be past his best, but a tribute is paid to his fine style. This brings out the important point that the Olympic Race will be a severe test of style, a point to which the selectors will give their fullest and most careful consideration. A Staines (Leicester W.C.) possesses good style as well as speed. Our own Coleman brothers too, will be in the reckoning. Four younger walkers, in H. G. Clayton (Belgrave), D. Kenney (Leicester W.C.), J. V. Sweeney (Metropolitan W.C.) and W. A. Webster (R.A.F., Halton) are also mentioned; Kenney gaining special mention as he is not yet twenty years old. To this Percy adds that he (no doubt like many others!) will try his hardest to gain Olympic colours. In conclusion, he predicts that the following will be the four from whom the team will be chosen: H. G. Churcher and J. G. Coleman (Belgrave), A. Staines and D. Kenney (Leicester W.C.). [Editor's Note.—This addition represents, of course, the personal views of P. G. Wright. Some will agree and some will differ, but nobody will doubt the honesty and sincerity of his views on a topic which can be so full of controversy]. S. C. Botwright S. C.
